description: BlueSky is an open-source air traffic simulator for research on air traffic management and air traffic flows. Written in Python with numpy, it simulates aircraft performance, the flight management system, autopilot, conflict detection and resolution and airborne separation, is extended through self-contained plugins, and is driven by console commands or time-stamped scenario files; it ships with open navaid, airport, geography and aircraft performance data and is compatible with BADA 3 data and NLR's Traffic Manager format. It is developed at TU Delft and described by Hoekstra and Ellerbroek at ICRAT 2016. Navaid and airport data give it global coverage, so scenarios can be built for any airspace. It is distributed under the MIT licence, free, via GitHub (tags up to 2024.07.01, commits into September 2026) and PyPI as bluesky-simulator, with a wiki for guides. Caveats: the developers call it perpetual beta, VNAV is still under construction, and performance data outside BADA is approximate. BlueSky is used for airspace capacity, conflict resolution, drone and urban air mobility traffic and disruption studies; it relates to OpenAP for aircraft performance and to OpenSky trajectories for scenario input, both catalogued here.
